mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_LeastPrivilege removes the constraint that a successful operation requires a permitted role. The injection forces an auditor-only user to succeed at PostApplications, which LeastPrivilege must catch because RApplicant -> PostApplications is in Allowed but RAuditor -> PostApplications is not.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some op: Operation | RAuditor in op.opCaller.userRoles and ROfficer not in op.opCaller.userRoles and RApplicant not in op.opCaller.userRoles and op.opKind = PostApplications and op.opOutcome = Success }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_AppendOnlyAuditEntries allows two AuditEntry atoms to share the same (app, prevStatus, newStatus, actor) tuple, modelling a 'replaced' entry — exactly what an UPDATE on audit_entries would produce. The injection forces such a duplicate to exist.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj e1, e2: AuditEntry | e1.entryApp = e2.entryApp and e1.entryPrevStatus = e2.entryPrevStatus and e1.entryNewStatus = e2.entryNewStatus and e1.entryActor = e2.entryActor }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_NoSelfApproval allows an officer to successfully PATCH an application where they are also the applicant. The injection forces exactly that configuration, which NoSelfMutation must detect.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_SelfApprovalViolation { some op: Operation | op.opKind = PatchApplicationStatus and op.opOutcome = Success and (one a: op.opApp | a.appApplicant = op.opCaller and a.appOfficer = op.opCaller) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_AuthRequiredEverywhere allows an unauthenticated caller (userRoles = empty) to receive Success. The injection forces a user with no roles to have a successful operation, which the auth assertions must catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthBypassViolation { some op: Operation | no op.opCaller.userRoles and op.opOutcome = Success }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_AuditCompleteness allows a successful state-changing operation to exist with no corresponding audit entry. The injection forces a successful PatchApplicationStatus with no AuditEntry linking to the same (app, caller) pair.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenessViolation { some op: Operation | op.opKind = PatchApplicationStatus and op.opOutcome = Success and (no e: AuditEntry | e.entryApp = op.opApp and e.entryActor = op.opCaller) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_NoInformationLeakage allows an authenticated non-success GET /applications/{id} to return Forbidden instead of NotFound, which distinguishes 'exists but denied' from 'not found' and violates the byte-equivalence invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_InfoLeakViolation { some op: Operation | op.opKind = GetApplicationById and some op.opCaller.userRoles and op.opOutcome = Forbidden }
